In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
statins are the first-line drugs for the prevention of cardiovascular disease in type 2 diabetes.
there are no clear data that the combination of statin therapy and fibrate therapy reduces the risk of cardiovascular events in patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes.
the use of combination lipid therapy is not supported by the available clinical trial evidence in patients with diabetes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we did not find any benefit for the use of a fibrate plus statin in type 2 diabetes.
the combination of simvastatin plus ezetimibe was superior to simvastatin monotherapy for the primary outcome of major cardiovascular events in the ACCORD Lipid Trial.
the use of combination therapies in the ACCORD Lipid Trial is not justified.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the setting of type 2 diabetes and high cardiovascular risk, the combination of simvastatin and ezetimibe, compared with simvastatin alone, reduced the risk of cardiovascular events.
the combination of a fibrate and a statin does not reduce cardiovascular events in patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes.
we need to do more to help patients with type 1 and 2 diabetes.
